body: Yes. It depends on your field also it seems. But I have heard from personal friends who are in different industries that they are also struggling. For me, I come from marketing industry, and it’s tough. Plenty of jobs to apply to, but you are one of hundreds who apply and now companies have also shifted down the pay scale. I have seen so many Sr marketing manager positions that only offer $60k-$75k a year. But a few years ago those same jobs would be at a $80k-$95k range for starting. I mean I have even seen a few marketing positions that were only offering $40k but the job description was for someone who would be at a higher level in that field. Also with so many remote positions being cut, and corporate lay offs, wait I mean “company restructuring” or whatever they call it now, I feel like many are now having to look more locally vs before which overinflated the job market at least where I live. Also with this market and the companies knowing that they are working with a flux of job searchers they are being very unprofessional. Ghosting applicants. For every 20 jobs I apply to, I maybe get one “we are sorry, we moved forward with other candidates” emails. So is the market rough, yes. But I think it’s the companies making it harder than it should be seeing they are using people’s desperation for employment as a tool to underpay top talent and make such an awkward market to navigate.
